One review states: "with almost 200 bottles of whiskys behind the bar, village whiskey has the largest single collection in all of philadelphia." This says "almost 200," which is less than 200, not over 200.

Another review mentions: "There are over 200 whiskeys available on the menu." This supports the claim of over 200.

Another review says: "they also have a great selection of whiskeys and bourbons, my personal favorite. It's in my mind the best in the city, though a bit on the expensive side. Their old fashioned is one of the best I've ever had..."

Another says: "did I mention they offer over 80+ different whiskeys?"

So we have conflicting information:
- One review says "almost 200 bottles"
- One review says "over 200 whiskeys"
- One review says "over 80+ different whiskeys"

The hint says to interpret the claim as an implicit universal quantification over all reviews that mention the number of whiskey varieties. This means ALL reviews that mention the number should support "over 200." But one review says "almost 200" (which contradicts "over 200") and another says "over 80+" (which doesn't necessarily contradict but doesn't confirm over 200 either).

Since not all reviews that mention the number agree with "over 200" - specifically the "almost 200" review contradicts it - the claim is not fully grounded in the dataset.
